les: Van 'n fietswinkel tot in die lug
kaps_punt: Wright broers en die uitvinding van die eerste vliegtuig

items.bewering: Wilbur en Orville Wright het hul eie fietswinkel in Amerika gehad.
items.bron: wright-brothers.org, Just the Facts: Wright Bicycles (Wright Cycle Exchange, 1005 West Third Street, Dayton, Ohio, 1892); NPS Dayton Aviation Heritage NHP, Wright Cycle Company (home.nps.gov/daav/learn/historyculture/wrightcyclecompany.htm).

items.bewering: Hulle het daar fietse herstel, verhuur en verkoop.
items.bron: wright-brothers.org, Wright Bicycles: 'a bicycle sales and repair shop' and 'The Wrights also rented bicycles and sold parts and accessories.' (The NPS page confirms sales but does not mention rentals; it does not contradict them.)

items.bewering: Later het hulle self fietse gebou.
items.bron: NPS, Wright Cycle Company: own brand designed from 1895, first bicycles ready for sale 16 May 1896 (Van Cleve, later St. Clair); The Henry Ford, Wright Cycle Company collection.

items.bewering: Daarom het hulle voëls in die lug fyn dopgehou. Hulle het gesien hoe 'n voël se vlerke buig en draai.
items.bron: wright-brothers.org, 'Warped Experiment'; NPS Historical Handbook 34 (nps.gov/parkhistory/online_books/hh/34/hh34e.htm): Wilbur's 1899 letter to the Smithsonian mentions his habit of watching birds, and his 1900 letter to Chanute describes buzzards regaining balance by twisting their wingtips. Note only: Orville later played down how much they learned from birds; the lesson's claim (they watched, they saw wings bend and twist) is still true.

items.bewering: Daarna het hulle self vlerke gebou wat 'n hele masjien kon dra.
items.bron: NASA Glenn, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics, 1900 glider page; wright-brothers.org: the 1899 wing-warping kite led to the 1900 glider, large enough to carry a person.

items.bewering: Die broers se eerste vliegtuig was 'n sweeftuig sonder 'n enjin. (Also the heading: 'Hul eerste vliegtuig was 'n sweeftuig'.)
items.bron: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide (1900 glider) and wright-brothers.org: their first full-size, piloted craft was the 1900 glider. Before it came the 1899 kite, about five feet across, which carried nobody. Under the lesson's own definition of 'vliegtuig' (a machine 'waarin 'n mens deur die lug reis') the claim holds. Afrikaans usage that counts a sweeftuig as a vliegtuig: af.wikipedia 'Sweeftuig' ('n tipe vliegtuig wat ... deur die lug kan sweef'). That is a secondary source; the WAT entry could not be reached.

items.bewering: 'n Sweeftuig het niks wat dit vorentoe stoot nie. Dit gly stadig al laer deur die lug om hom.
items.bron: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide, 'Unpowered aircraft': a glider has no thrust. Cambridge University Gliding Club, 'How Gliders Fly', and Wikipedia 'Ridge lift': a glider always descends relative to the surrounding air at its sink rate. 'deur die lug om hom' correctly makes the descent relative to the air.

items.bewering: Teen 'n heuwel stoot die wind die lug self boontoe. Dan kan die sweeftuig in die lug bly en selfs hoër klim.
items.bron: British Gliding Association, 'Lift Sources' (gliding.co.uk); Wikipedia 'Ridge lift': wind blowing against a hill is forced upward (orographic lift), and a glider in that rising air holds or gains height when the updraft exceeds its sink rate. Consistent with the previous sentence: the glider still sinks through the air, and the air itself rises.

items.bewering: Die broers moes dikwels wag vir die regte wind voordat hulle kon vlieg.
items.bron: NPS Wright Brothers National Memorial, 'Wind, Sand, Isolation' (nps.gov/places/2-wind-sand-isolation.htm): steady wind was their first criterion for the site. Orville Wright's diary, 12 December 1903 (ECU digital exhibit): 'did not have enough wind for starting from flat'. National Geographic: on 16 December 1903 they waited another 24 hours for wind.

items.bewering: Op hul sweeftuie het hulle geleer om 'n masjien in die lug te stuur.
items.bron: NPS Historical Handbook 34 (hh34j); airandspaceforces.com 'Dawn at Kill Devil Hill': through more than a thousand glides the Wrights made themselves the first true pilots before powered flight.

items.bewering: Om te vlieg is nie net om van die grond af op te styg nie. Jy moet ook kan draai, en jy moet die vliegtuig reguit kan hou.
items.blok: Vlieg is meer as net opstyg
items.bron: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide (1902 glider): the Wrights treated control of all three axes (roll, pitch, yaw) as the problem to solve. Smithsonian NASM: 'controlled, sustained flight'.

items.bewering: Beheer beteken dat die vlieënier self besluit waarheen die vliegtuig se neus wys. Op hul sweeftuig van 1902 kon die vlieënier self die neus draai.
items.blok: Vlieg is meer as net opstyg
items.bron: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide, 1902 glider: 'the first aircraft in the world that had active controls for all three axis'. wright-brothers.org, 1902 Glider: the pilot moved the nose up and down with the front elevator, and from early October 1902 a movable rudder swung it from side to side. The rudder was linked to the hip cradle, so the pilot still controlled where the nose pointed.

items.bewering: Hulle het honderde vlugte daarmee gemaak voordat hulle 'n enjin gehad het.
items.blok: Vlieg is meer as net opstyg
items.bron: Britannica, 'Wright glider of 1902': 700–1,000 flights between 19 September and 24 October 1902, and a further 60–100 in autumn 1903 before the powered Flyer. Smithsonian Air & Space gives the same 700–1,000 range.

items.bewering: Hul langste glyvlug in 1902 het 26 sekondes geduur.
items.blok: Vlieg is meer as net opstyg
items.bron: Britannica, 'Wright glider of 1902': distances up to 622.5 ft (189.74 m), aloft up to 26 seconds. Franklin Institute, Wright Notebooks: the 622.5 ft, 26 s glide was on 23 October 1902.

items.bewering: So 'n vlug het van 'n sandduin af begin en op die grond geëindig.
items.blok: Vlieg is meer as net opstyg
items.bron: NPS Historical Handbook 34 (hh34j); NPS 'Wind, Sand, Isolation': the glides were launched from the sand slopes of the Kill Devil Hills dunes.

items.bewering: 'n Sweeftuig sak deur die lug om hom. Hy moet dus eers hoogte kry voordat hy kan gly. Die broers het daarvoor 'n duin of 'n heuwel gebruik. Hul glyvlugte was verby sodra daardie hoogte opgebruik was.
items.bron: NPS 'Wind, Sand, Isolation' (high dunes to glide from); Britannica, 'Wright glider of 1902'; airandspaceforces.com 'Dawn at Kill Devil Hill' (glides from the sand slopes lasted 10 to 15 seconds). Consistent with the ridge-lift sentences in block 2: a rising wind can stretch a glide, but every Wright glide still ended once its height was used up.

items.bewering: 'n Enjin verander brandstof se energie in beweging. Daarom kan 'n vliegtuig homself vorentoe stoot in plaas daarvan om af te gly.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'engine': a machine that changes energy (such as heat from burning fuel) into mechanical motion. NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide: the engine turns the propellers, which give the thrust a glider lacks. Shortening engine → propeller → thrust to 'stoot homself vorentoe' is acceptable at Grade 4.

items.bewering: 'n Vlug met 'n enjin is nie verby sodra die beginhoogte op is nie. Die vlug eindig wanneer die vlieënier land.
items.bron: Follows from the engine giving thrust (Britannica, NASA Glenn as above). Shown in practice by the Wright Flyer III's 39-minute circling flight of 5 October 1905, which ended when the fuel tank ran low (wright-brothers.org, Flyer III).

items.bewering: Op 17 Desember 1903 het hulle 'n vliegtuig met 'n enjin laat opstyg. Een van die broers was self aan boord, en hy kon die vliegtuig stuur.
items.bron: Smithsonian NASM, 1903 Wright Flyer object record (si.edu); NPS 'Four Powered Flights' (home.nps.gov/places/3-four-powered-flights.htm): four flights on 17 December 1903, with the brothers taking turns at the controls.

items.bewering: Dit was die eerste suksesvolle vlug van 'n vliegtuig met 'n enjin wat 'n mens kon beheer.
items.bron: Smithsonian NASM, 1903 Wright Flyer: 'the first powered, heavier-than-air machine to achieve controlled, sustained flight with a pilot aboard'. NASA, '120 years ago: the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk'. The lesson keeps both qualifiers, engine and control, and 'vliegtuig' already excludes earlier powered airships. Competing claims (Whitehead 1901) are not accepted by mainstream aviation history.

items.bewering: Die langste vlug van daardie dag was minder as 'n minuut lank. Die vlugte was dus nog kort.
items.bron: Smithsonian NASM: best flight of the day, Wilbur, 852 ft in 59 seconds. NPS 'Four Powered Flights': first flight 12 s and 120 ft, third 15 s and 200 ft, fourth 59 s and 852 ft.

items.bewering: Die enjin het wel gesorg dat die vliegtuig van plat grond af kon opstyg.
items.bron: NPS 'Four Powered Flights': the launching rail was laid on level ground, pointed into the wind. Orville's diary, 12 December 1903: 'not enough wind for starting from flat'. Note for a person, not a fault: a strong headwind (about 20–27 mph) was also needed that day. The sentence is right as a contrast with a glider, which needs a dune; it should not be expanded to say the engine alone was enough.

items.bewering: Ná die eerste vlug (block heading)
items.bron: The lesson itself, block 'Vlieg is meer as net opstyg': 'Hulle het honderde vlugte daarmee gemaak voordat hulle 'n enjin gehad het' (Britannica: 700–1,000 glides in 1902). The 17 December 1903 flight was not the brothers' first flight. Only qualified is it first: the first powered, controlled flight (Smithsonian NASM).
items.regstelling: The heading drops the qualifiers that block '17 Desember 1903' keeps, so on its own it teaches the popular error that 1903 was the first flight of all. The lesson's own count of hundreds of earlier glides contradicts it. The heading must name the 1903 flight as the first flight WITH AN ENGINE, or name it by its year, not call it 'die eerste vlug' unqualified.

items.bewering: In die jare kort ná 1903 het vliegtuie baie vinnig beter geword. Al hoe meer mense het vliegtuie gebou en self leer vlieg.
items.bron: wright-brothers.org, 'The Decade After: Nov 1905 to Oct 1909'; American Heritage, 'How Wilbur Wright taught Europe to fly': Santos-Dumont's records in 1906, Farman's closed-circuit kilometre in 1908, Wilbur's demonstrations at Le Mans in 1908, and the Reims meet in 1909.

items.bewering: Nuwe enjins was sterker, en vlieëniers kon hul masjiene beter beheer. Vliegtuie kon ook al hoe langer in die lug bly. 'n Vliegtuig kon hoër klim en verder vlieg as die een van 1903.
items.bron: wright-brothers.org, Flyer III: 39.5 minutes and 24 miles on 5 October 1905. Wilbur flew over 2 h 20 min on 31 December 1908. The Gnome rotary engine (50 hp) appeared in 1908 and won at Reims in 1909, against the 1903 Flyer's roughly 12 hp (wright-brothers.org, 'The Decade After'; earlyaviators.com).

items.bewering: So het twee broers wat fietse herstel het, van die lug 'n pad gemaak.
items.bron: The underlying facts are confirmed above: they repaired bicycles (wright-brothers.org) and made the first powered, controlled flight (Smithsonian NASM). Mapping checked: 'die lug as 'n pad' maps onto air as a route for travel, which suits a transport topic. The risk is over-crediting, as if two brothers alone turned the sky into a road, but the sentence before it ('Al hoe meer mense het vliegtuie gebou') already brings in the many others. A learner reasoning further would not be led astray.

items.bewering: sweeftuig: 'n Vliegtuig wat sonder 'n enjin deur die lug om hom afgly.
items.bron: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide, 'Unpowered aircraft'; af.wikipedia 'Sweeftuig' ('n tipe vliegtuig). 'om hom afgly' (sinking relative to the surrounding air) agrees with ridge lift: Cambridge University Gliding Club, 'How Gliders Fly'.

items.bewering: vlerk: Die deel van 'n voël of 'n vliegtuig waarmee dit vlieg.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster, 'wing': the paired appendages by which a bird, bat or insect flies, and the part extending from the side of an airplane. The list leaves out bats and insects but makes no false contrast.

items.bewering: enjin: 'n Masjien wat energie in beweging verander.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'engine'; Dictionary.com (scientific): a machine that converts energy into mechanical force or motion.

items.bewering: vliegtuig: 'n Masjien met vlerke waarin 'n mens deur die lug reis.
items.bron: af.wikipedia 'Vliegtuig': 'n masjien wat in staat is tot atmosferiese vlugte, with no engine required. Merriam-Webster 'wing' (aircraft sense). The definition does not require an engine, which matches the lesson calling a sweeftuig a vliegtuig. Its 'waarin 'n mens ... reis' is what makes the 1900 glider, not the unmanned 1899 kite, the brothers' first vliegtuig. Note only: no WAT or HAT entry could be reached to confirm the formal Afrikaans sense.

opsomming: Elke feitelike bewering hou teen die bronne, insluitend die drie superlatiewe in die studieteks: die 26 sekondes van 1902, die 59 sekondes van 1903 en die eerste beheerde enjinvlug. Een opskrif, 'Ná die eerste vlug', laat egter die kwalifiseerders weg en noem die vlug van 1903 die eerste vlug. Dit weerspreek die les se eie 'honderde vlugte' met die sweeftuig voor 1903 en moet as die eerste vlug met 'n enjin benoem word.
